findings.title: SQL injection in search_orders_advanced via f-string
findings.explanation: User-controlled `query` is interpolated directly into SQL with f"... LIKE '%{query}%'", allowing SQL injection to read/modify arbitrary data. Must use bound parameter.

evidence.why: User input interpolated directly into SQL string via f-string

findings.suggestion: Use parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT ... WHERE status LIKE ?", (f"%{query}%",)) instead of f-string.

findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-user order search endpoint
findings.explanation: New GET /orders/search2 takes only `q` with no `user` and calls search_orders_advanced across all users' orders, unlike existing /orders/search which scopes by user. Exposes other users' orders.

evidence.why: New endpoint takes only q with no user auth, unlike scoped search
Helper explicitly searches across all users orders by status

findings.suggestion: Require authenticated `user` and scope query by user_name, or remove endpoint if not needed.

findings.title: Hardcoded AWS secret key in source
findings.explanation: RECEIPT_AWS_KEY is hardcoded in new uploads module, leaking credential via repo history and builds. Secrets must not live in code.

evidence.why: AWS secret hardcoded as source constant

findings.suggestion: Remove key from source; load from environment/secret manager and rotate exposed credential.
